theorem mean_laplacian_commutes (q : XiZeroCopy) (d x k : ℝ) :
    (Real.exp k:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q d r k)) x+

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hx := horizontal_family q d k
  have hk := height_family q d x
  have hxx := second_slice_continuous hx x
  have hkk := second_slice_continuous hk k
  have hk1 := first_slice_continuous hk k
  have hg := horizontal_theta_smooth q d x k
  have hgp := (smooth_derivative hg).continuous
  have hz := average_periodic_derivative hg (horizontal_theta_periodic q d x k)
  have hQ : (fun theta => coordDeriv 0 (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k))=
      fun theta => deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k) x :=
    funext (fun theta => (source_horizontal_derivative q d theta x k).symm)
  have he (theta : ℝ) : scalarLaplacian (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k)=
      (Real.exp k:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k)) x+
      deriv (deriv (fun r => source q d theta x r)) k-deriv (fun r => source q d theta x r) k+
      2*(Real.exp k:ℂ)*deriv (fun t => deriv (fun r => source q d t r k) x) theta := by
    have h := source_base_laplacian_integrand q d theta x k
    rw [hQ] at h
    linear_combination -h
  have h := congrArg average (funext he)
  erw [average_add (((hxx.const_mul ((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2)).add hkk).sub hk1)
      (hgp.const_mul (2*(Real.exp k:ℂ))),
    average_sub ((hxx.const_mul ((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2)).add hkk) hk1,
    average_add (hxx.const_mul ((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2)) hkk,
    average_const_mul,average_const_mul,hz,mul_zero,add_zero] at h
  rw [← average_second hx x,← average_second hk k,← average_derivative hk k] at h
  exact h.symm

            (deningerArithmeticGradedSourceReal a) := by
      calc
        deningerArithmeticGradedWeilTransport a =
            deningerArithmeticGradedWeilTransport

          rw [deningerArithmeticGradedSourceReal_sq]
        _ = deningerArithmeticGradedHodgeStar

    have hWTheta :

            (deningerArithmeticGradedSourceReal

    (F : LocalField.{u, v} K)

    equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation F n

          F u n)
        (equalCharacteristicThetaSeriesFrobenius u) =

by
  let root := equalCharacteristicCompletedPrimitiveRootInteger F n
  let hroot := equalCharacteristicCompletedPrimitiveRootInteger_hasEval F n
  let source := equalCharacteristicCompletedLubinTateSeries
    (equalCharacteristicCompletedSourceUniformizer u)
  let theta := equalCharacteristicThetaSeries u
  let target := equalCharacteristicCompletedLubinTateSeries
    (k := F.residueField) PowerSeries.X
  have hleft := equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation_subst F n
    source (equalCharacteristicThetaSeriesFrobenius u)
    (equalCharacteristicCompletedLubinTateSeries_hasSubst
      (equalCharacteristicCompletedSourceUniformizer u))
    hroot
    (equalCharacteristicSourceLubinTateAtCompletedPrimitiveRoot_hasEval F u n)
  have hright := equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation_subst F n
    theta target (equalCharacteristicThetaSeries_hasSubst u) hroot
    (equalCharacteristicThetaAtCompletedPrimitiveRoot_hasEval F u n)
  have hintertwines := congrArg
    (equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation F n root hroot)
    (equalCharacteristicThetaSeries_intertwines u)
  calc
    _ = equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation F n root hroot
        (PowerSeries.subst source
          (equalCharacteristicThetaSeriesFrobenius u)) := by
          simpa [equalCharacteristicSourceLubinTateAtCompletedPrimitiveRoot,
            source, root, hroot] using hleft.symm
    _ = equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation F n root hroot
        (PowerSeries.subst theta target) := by
          simpa [source, theta, target] using hintertwines
    _ = equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelEvaluation F n
        (equalCharacteristicThetaAtCompletedPrimitiveRoot F u n)
        (equalCharacteristicThetaAtCompletedPrimitiveRoot_hasEval F u n)
        target := by
          simpa [equalCharacteristicThetaAtCompletedPrimitiveRoot,
            theta, root, hroot] using hright
    _ = _ := by
      simp [target, equalCharacteristicCompletedLubinTateSeries,
        equalCharacteristicCompletedLevelUniformizerInteger]

  by simpa only [mean_eq] using mean_laplacian_commutes q branch d x k

private theorem theta_smooth (q : XiZeroCopy) (branch : Bool) (d x k : ℝ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun theta => source q branch d theta x k) := by
  apply contDiff_iff_contDiffAt.mpr
  intro theta
  have hp : 0 < logCircle d theta x k 1 := logCircle_pos d theta x k
  have hs : ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ (fullAngularField q branch) (logCircle d theta x k) :=
    fullAngularField_smooth q branch _ hp
  apply hs.comp theta
  apply contDiffAt_pi.mpr
  intro i
  fin_cases i <;> dsimp [logCircle,circle,offset,height,denominator]
  all_goals fun_prop (disch := exact (denominator_pos _ _).ne')

/-- The base action of the actual full angular mean retains the complete theta forcing. -/

al_action (q : XiZeroCopy) (d x k : ℝ) :
    (Real.sinh d:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q r x k)) d+
      (Real.sinh d:ℂ)*(Real.cosh d:ℂ)*deriv (fun r => mean q r x k) d=
      (Real.sinh d:ℂ)^2*average (fun theta =>
        scalarLaplacian (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k)) := by
  have hf := radial_family q x k
  have hr := first_slice_continuous hf d
  have hrr := second_slice_continuous hf d
  have ht := theta_smooth q d x k
  have htt := (smooth_derivative (smooth_derivative ht)).continuous
  have hz : average (deriv (deriv (fun theta => source q d theta x k)))=0 :=
    average_periodic_derivative (smooth_derivative ht) (periodic_derivative ht (source_periodic q d x k))
  have h := congrArg average (funext (fun theta => source_darboux_integrand q d theta x k))
  erw [average_add ((hrr.const_mul ((Real.sinh d:ℂ)^2)).add
      (hr.const_mul ((Real.sinh d:ℂ)*(Real.cosh d:ℂ)))) htt,
    average_add (hrr.const_mul ((Real.sinh d:ℂ)^2))
      (hr.const_mul ((Real.sinh d:ℂ)*(Real.cosh d:ℂ))),average_const_mul,average_const_mul,
    average_const_mul,hz,add_zero] at h
  rw [← average_second hf d,← average_derivative hf d] at h
  exact h

private theorem horizontal_theta_smooth (q : XiZeroCopy) (d x k : ℝ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun theta => deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k) x) := by
  have he : (fun theta => deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k) x)=
      fun theta => coordDeriv 0 (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k) :=
    funext (fun theta => source_horizontal_derivative q d theta x k)
  rw [he]
  apply contDiff_iff_contDiffAt.mpr
  intro theta
  have hp : 0 < logCircle d theta x k 1 := by
    exact mul_pos (Real.exp_pos _) (one_div_pos.mpr (denominator_pos _ _))
  have hs : ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k) :=
    contDiffAt_infty.mpr (fun n => fullSquarePotential_smooth q _ hp n)
  apply (coordDeriv_contDiffAt (m := ∞) (by simpa using hs) 0).comp theta
  apply contDiffAt_pi.mpr
  intro i
  fin_cases i <;> dsimp [logCircle,circle,offset,height,denominator]
  all_goals fun_prop (disch := exact (denominator_pos _ _).ne')

private theorem horizontal_theta_periodic (q : XiZeroCopy) (d x k theta : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun r => source q d (theta+2*Real.pi) r k) x=
      deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k) x :=
  congrArg (fun f : ℝ → ℂ => deriv f x) (funext (fun r => source_periodic q d r k theta))

/-- The actual base-point Laplacian commutes with averaging the complete original theta half-square. -/
theorem mean_laplacian_commutes (q : XiZeroCopy) (d x k : ℝ) :
    (Real.exp k:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q d r k)) x+
      deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q d x r)) k-deriv (fun r => mean q d x r) k=
      average (fun theta => scalarLaplacian (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k)) := by
  have hx := horizontal_family q d k
  have hk := height_family q d x
  have hxx := second_slice_continuous hx x
  have hkk := second_slice_continuous hk k
  have hk1 := first_slice_continuous hk k
  have hg := horizontal_theta_smooth q d x k
  have hgp := (smooth_derivative hg).continuous
  have hz := average_periodic_derivative hg (horizontal_theta_periodic q d x k)
  have hQ : (fun theta => coordDeriv 0 (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k))=
      fun theta => deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k) x :=
    funext (fun theta => (source_horizontal_derivative q d theta x k).symm)
  have he (theta : ℝ) : scalarLaplacian (fullSquarePotential q) (logCircle d theta x k)=
      (Real.exp k:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => source q d theta r k)) x+
      deriv (deriv (fun r => source q d theta x r)) k-deriv (fun r => source q d theta x r) k+
      2*(Real.exp k:ℂ)*deriv (fun t => deriv (fun r => source q d t r k) x) theta := by
    have h := source_base_laplacian_integrand q d theta x k
    rw [hQ] at h
    linear_combination -h
  have h := congrArg average (funext he)
  erw [average_add (((hxx.const_mul ((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2)).add hkk).sub hk1)
      (hgp.const_mul (2*(Real.exp k:ℂ))),
    average_sub ((hxx.const_mul ((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2)).add hkk) hk1,
    average_add (hxx.const_mul ((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2)) hkk,
    average_const_mul,average_const_mul,hz,mul_zero,add_zero] at h
  rw [← average_second hx x,← average_second hk k,← average_derivative hk k] at h
  exact h.symm

/-- The full native theta circle average solves the original hyperbolic Darboux equation. -/
theorem mean_darboux (q : XiZeroCopy) (d x k : ℝ) :
    (Real.sinh d:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q r x k)) d+
      (Real.sinh d:ℂ)*(Real.cosh d:ℂ)*deriv (fun r => mean q r x k) d=
      (Real.sinh d:ℂ)^2*((Real.exp k:ℂ)^2*deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q d r k)) x+
        deriv (deriv (fun r => mean q d x r)) k-deriv (fun r => mean q d x r) k) := by
  rw [mean_radial_action,mean_laplacian_commutes]

private theorem average_constant (c : ℂ) : average (fun _ => c)=c := by
  have hT : 0 ≤ 2*Real.pi := by positivity
  have hpi : (Real.pi:ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr Real.pi_ne_zero
  dsimp [average]

  have hfirst :=

      (n := 1) (by norm_num) hx.le).neg
  have hhigher := hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFour
    (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate_pos hx.le)

  have heq : iteratedDeriv 5 thetaCuspLogSource =ᶠ[nhds x]
      thetaCuspFullLogJetFive := by
    filter_upwards [Ioi_mem_nhds hx] with y hy
    exact iteratedDeriv_five_thetaCuspLogSource_eq_full_jets hy
  have hfirst :=
    (hasDerivAt_thetaCuspBornWittenLogFifthDerivative
      (n := 1) (by norm_num) hx.le).neg
  have hhigher := hasDerivAt_thetaCuspLikelihoodSourceLogPartitionJetFive
    (thetaCuspLikelihoodCoordinate_pos hx.le)

    unfold thetaCuspFullLogJetFive thetaCuspFullLogJetSix
    exact hfirst.add hhigher
  rw [show 6 = 5 + 1 by norm_num, iteratedDeriv_succ]

/-- Positive-coordinate form of the actual sixth logarithmic source jet. -/

          iteratedDeriv 4 thetaCuspLogSource x +

      thetaCuspFullReflectionSixthCurvature x := by
  rw [iteratedDeriv_two_thetaCuspLogSource_eq_factor hx,
    iteratedDeriv_four_thetaCuspLogSource_eq_factor hx,
    iteratedDeriv_six_thetaCuspLogSource_eq_full_jets hx,

/-!
# Mode-gauge holonomy of a thermal-horizon Bogoliubov kernel

A complex Bogoliubov kernel depends on independent conventions for incoming and outgoing mode
phases.  The alternating phase around a frequency rectangle cancels every output-only and
input-only phase.  Exponentiating gives the corresponding multiplicative kernel holonomy.

For the ideal thermal-horizon carrier, use outgoing frequency `x` and logarithmic incoming
frequency `ℓ`.  Its coupled phase is

`-i * inverseSurfaceGravity * x * ℓ`.

The rectangular defect is exactly

`-i * inverseSurfaceGravity * (x₁-x₂) * (ℓ₁-ℓ₂)`.

Consequently any frequency-row factor, including a Gamma phase depending only on outgoing
frequency, cancels from this fully separable-gauge-invariant observable.  This is an algebraic
statement about the stated kernel.  It does not assert that arbitrary frequency-dependent mode
rephasings are the physically preferred calibration, nor that exact exponential peeling holds for
every horizon.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Additive alternating defect around an input-output rectangle. -/
def rectanglePhaseDefect
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) : ℂ :=
  phase x₁ y₁ + phase x₂ y₂ - phase x₁ y₂ - phase x₂ y₁

/-- Independent row and column phase conventions cancel from the rectangular defect. -/
theorem rectanglePhaseDefect_separableGauge
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (row : X → ℂ) (column : Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) :
    rectanglePhaseDefect
        (fun x y => row x + phase x y + column y) x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ =
      rectanglePhaseDefect phase x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ := by
  simp only [rectanglePhaseDefect]
  ring

/-- Coupled phase of the ideal exponential-peeling horizon kernel in outgoing frequency and
logarithmic incoming frequency. -/
def thermalHorizonPhaseExponent
    (inverseSurfaceGravity outgoingFrequency logIncomingFrequency : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  -Complex.I * inverseSurfaceGravity * outgoingFrequency * logIncomingFrequency

/-- The unwrapped rectangular phase defect recovers the inverse-surface-gravity coefficient. -/
theorem rectanglePhaseDefect_thermalHorizonPhaseExponent
    (inverseSurfaceGravity x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℂ) :
    rectanglePhaseDefect
        (thermalHorizonPhaseExponent inverseSurfaceGravity) x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ =
      -Complex.I * inverseSurfaceGravity * (x₁ - x₂) * (ℓ₁ - ℓ₂) := by
  simp only [rectanglePhaseDefect, thermalHorizonPhaseExponent]
  ring

/-- Multiplicative alternating holonomy around an input-output rectangle. -/
def rectangleKernelHolonomy
    {X Y : Type*} (kernel : X → Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) : ℂ :=
  kernel x₁ y₁ * kernel x₂ y₂ /
    (kernel x₁ y₂ * kernel x₂ y₁)

/-- Exponential kernel generated by an additive phase. -/
def exponentialKernel
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ) : X → Y → ℂ :=
  fun x y => Complex.exp (phase x y)

/-- Rectangle holonomy of an exponential kernel is the exponential of its phase defect. -/
theorem rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) :
    rectangleKernelHolonomy (exponentialKernel phase) x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ =
      Complex.exp (rectanglePhaseDefect phase x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂) := by
  simp only [rectangleKernelHolonomy, exponentialKernel, rectanglePhaseDefect]
  rw [← Complex.exp_add, ← Complex.exp_add, ← Complex.exp_sub]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- Multiplicative rectangle holonomy is invariant under arbitrary separable exponential mode
calibrations. -/
theorem rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponential_separableGauge
    {X Y : Type*} (phase : X → Y → ℂ)
    (row : X → ℂ) (column : Y → ℂ)
    (x₁ x₂ : X) (y₁ y₂ : Y) :
    rectangleKernelHolonomy
        (exponentialKernel (fun x y => row x + phase x y + column y))
        x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ =
      rectangleKernelHolonomy (exponentialKernel phase) x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ := by
  rw [rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel,
    rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel,
    rectanglePhaseDefect_separableGauge]

/-- Exact thermal-horizon rectangle holonomy.  Unlike the one-frequency Gamma phase, this
separable-gauge quotient contains only the coupled surface-gravity phase. -/
theorem rectangleKernelHolonomy_thermalHorizon
    (inverseSurfaceGravity x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ : ℂ) :
    rectangleKernelHolonomy
        (exponentialKernel
          (thermalHorizonPhaseExponent inverseSurfaceGravity))
        x₁ x₂ ℓ₁ ℓ₂ =
      Complex.exp
        (-Complex.I * inverseSurfaceGravity *
          (x₁ - x₂) * (ℓ₁ - ℓ₂)) := by
  rw [rectangleKernelHolonomy_exponentialKernel,
    rectanglePhaseDefect_thermalHorizonPhaseExponent]

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# The Xi Gamma-shape trace is completely monotone on its safe interval

The nonnegative Xi prime-seam trace is a general Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients and
nonnegative frequencies.  On its safe shape interval every alternating derivative is the
corresponding nonnegative frequency moment, and the radial Hankel kernel is a Gram kernel of
exponential vectors.

Complete monotonicity is strictly stronger than plain Hankel positivity: the kernel
`K(s,t) = exp (s + t)` is a rank-one Gram kernel, yet the real exponential is not completely
monotone because its generator frequency is negative.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- **Complete monotonicity on the safe shape interval.**  Every alternating derivative of the
global Gamma-shape trace is the corresponding nonnegative frequency moment. -/
theorem xiGammaShapeTrace_completelyMonotone {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 < θ) (k : ℕ) :
    ((-1) ^ k * iteratedDeriv k xiGammaShapeTrace ((θ : ℝ) : ℂ)) =
      ((GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdMoment
        xiGammaShapeCoefficient xiGammaShapeFrequency θ k : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  set σ₁ : ℝ := (1 + θ) / 2 with hσ₁
  have hσ₁gt : 1 < σ₁ := by rw [hσ₁]; linarith
  have hh : 0 < θ - σ₁ := by rw [hσ₁]; linarith
  have hsplit : σ₁ + (θ - σ₁) = θ := by ring
  have h := GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdSeries_completelyMonotone
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient_nonneg xiGammaShapeFrequency_nonneg
    (summable_xiGammaShapeTwist hσ₁gt) hh k
  rw [hsplit] at h
  exact h

/-- The alternating derivatives are nonnegative reals. -/
theorem xiGammaShapeTrace_alternating_nonneg {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 1 < θ) (k : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ ((-1) ^ k * iteratedDeriv k xiGammaShapeTrace ((θ : ℝ) : ℂ)).re := by
  rw [xiGammaShapeTrace_completelyMonotone hθ k, Complex.ofReal_re]
  exact GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdMoment_nonneg
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient_nonneg xiGammaShapeFrequency_nonneg θ k

/-- The real Gamma-shape trace on the safe interval. -/
def xiGammaShapeRealTrace (θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdRealSeries
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient xiGammaShapeFrequency θ

/-- **Radial Hankel positivity.**  On the safe shape interval the Hankel kernel of the global
Gamma-shape trace is a Gram kernel of exponential vectors, hence positive semidefinite. -/
theorem xiGammaShapeRealTrace_hankel_nonneg {n : ℕ} (θ c : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hθ : ∀ i, 1 < θ i) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * xiGammaShapeRealTrace (θ i + θ j) * c j := by
  refine GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.gdRealSeries_hankel_nonneg
    xiGammaShapeCoefficient_nonneg xiGammaShapeFrequency_nonneg
    (summable_xiGammaShapeTwist (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 3 / 2)) θ c (fun i => ?_)
  linarith [hθ i]

/-! ## Plain Hankel positivity is strictly weaker -/

/-- The exponential kernel is a rank-one Gram kernel, hence positive semidefinite. -/
theorem exp_hankel_nonneg {n : ℕ} (θ c : Fin n → ℝ) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * Real.exp (θ i + θ j) * c j := by
  have hkey : ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * Real.exp (θ i + θ j) * c j =
      (∑ i, c i * Real.exp (θ i)) ^ 2 := by
    rw [sq, Finset.sum_mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
    rw [Real.exp_add]
    ring
  rw [hkey]
  exact sq_nonneg _

/-- The exponential is not completely monotone: its first alternating derivative is negative.
Positive semidefiniteness of the Hankel kernel therefore does not imply complete monotonicity. -/
theorem exp_not_completelyMonotone (θ : ℝ) :
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ 1 * iteratedDeriv 1 Real.exp θ < 0 := by
  have hderiv : iteratedDeriv 1 Real.exp θ = Real.exp θ := by
    rw [iteratedDeriv_one, Real.deriv_exp]
  rw [hderiv]
  simp only [pow_one]
  nlinarith [Real.exp_pos θ]

end

end RHTower

/-!
# The characteristic Evans boundary state has infinite rank

Three exact mechanisms of the card are formalized.

*The exterior trace is a Hankel kernel.*  With `s = x - a` and `t = a - y` one has `x - y = s + t`
exactly, so the columns of the exterior trace map are precisely the **translates** of the kernel.

*Finite rank forces an exponential polynomial.*  If every Hankel column lies in one
finite-dimensional space, the translation span of the kernel is finite-dimensional, and the
Anselone–Korevaar equivalence of `AnseloneKorevaarTranslationRank` — the continuous form of
Kronecker's finite-rank Hankel theorem — makes the kernel an exponential polynomial.  It then has
finitely many frequencies and extends to an **entire** function.  Contrapositively, a kernel with no
entire extension has infinite exterior rank.

*The Gamma pole lattice is infinite.*  The digamma arguments `1/4 ± i z/2` hit a nonpositive integer
exactly on `z = ± i(2n + 1/2)`; that lattice is infinite, so it is not the zero set of any nonzero
polynomial and the corrected symbol is not rational.

The analytic ingredients — the distribution kernel of `c_a(D)`, the meromorphic continuation of the
Gamma symbol and the identification of the Laplace transform of the kernel with a half-plane branch
of `c_a` — are cited parents and stay outside the Lean statement.
-/

open Complex

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## The exterior trace is a Hankel kernel -/

/-- **Equation (5) → (6).**  The exterior displacement splits exactly into the two boundary
coordinates `s = x - a` and `t = a - y`. -/
theorem exterior_displacement_split (a x y : ℝ) : x - y = (x - a) + (a - y) := by ring

/-- The `s`-th column of the Hankel kernel `k(s+t)`. -/
def hankelColumn (k : ℝ → ℂ) (s : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ := fun t => k (s + t)

/-- **Equation (6).**  The Hankel columns are exactly the translates of the kernel. -/
theorem hankelColumn_eq_realTranslate (k : ℝ → ℂ) (s : ℝ) :
    hankelColumn k s = realTranslate (-s) k := by
  funext t
  simp only [hankelColumn, realTranslate, sub_neg_eq_add]
  rw [add_comm]

/-! ## Finite rank forces an exponential polynomial -/

/-- **Section 3, Kronecker step.**  If every Hankel column lies in one finite-dimensional space,
the kernel is an exponential polynomial. -/
theorem mem_expPolySpace_of_hankelColumns {k : ℝ → ℂ} (hk : Continuous k)
    {V : Submodule ℂ (ℝ → ℂ)} [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (hcol : ∀ s : ℝ, hankelColumn k s ∈ V) : k ∈ expPolySpace := by
  refine (mem_expPolySpace_iff_finiteDimensional_translationSpan hk).mpr ?_
  have hle : translationSpan k ≤ V := by
    rw [translationSpan, Submodule.span_le]
    rintro u ⟨a, rfl⟩
    have hmem := hcol (-a)
    rw [hankelColumn_eq_realTranslate, neg_neg] at hmem
    exact hmem
  exact Submodule.finiteDimensional_of_le hle

/-- **Equation (7).**  A finite-rank Hankel kernel is a finite sum of blocks: finitely many
frequencies, each with a polynomial factor. -/
theorem exists_finite_frequencies {k : ℝ → ℂ} (hk : k ∈ expPolySpace) :
    ∃ (S : Finset ℂ) (P : ℂ → Polynomial ℂ), k = ∑ μ ∈ S, polyExp (P μ) μ := by
  obtain ⟨N, S, hmem⟩ := exists_expMonomialSpace_of_mem_expPolySpace hk
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := expMonomialSpace_le_blockSpan N S hmem
  exact ⟨S, P, hP⟩

/-- **Section 3, regularity step.**  A finite-rank Hankel kernel extends to an entire function: an
exponential polynomial has no singularity at all. -/
theorem exists_entire_extension_of_hankelColumns {k : ℝ → ℂ} (hk : Continuous k)
    {V : Submodule ℂ (ℝ → ℂ)} [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (hcol : ∀ s : ℝ, hankelColumn k s ∈ V) :
    ∃ K : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticOnNhd ℂ K (Set.univ : Set ℂ) ∧ ∀ x : ℝ, K (x : ℂ) = k x := by
  obtain ⟨K, hKmem, hKeq⟩ := exists_entire_extension (mem_expPolySpace_of_hankelColumns hk hcol)
  exact ⟨K, analyticOnNhd_of_mem_expPolySpaceC hKmem, hKeq⟩

/-- **The infinite-rank theorem.**  A continuous kernel admitting no entire extension has no
finite-dimensional space containing all of its Hankel columns: the exterior trace map has infinite
rank. -/
theorem not_hankelColumns_finiteDimensional {k : ℝ → ℂ} (hk : Continuous k)
    (hno : ∀ K : ℂ → ℂ, (∀ x : ℝ, K (x : ℂ) = k x) → ¬ AnalyticOnNhd ℂ K (Set.univ : Set ℂ))
    (V : Submodule ℂ (ℝ → ℂ)) [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] :
    ¬ (∀ s : ℝ, hankelColumn k s ∈ V) := by
  intro hcol
  obtain ⟨K, hKan, hKeq⟩ := exists_entire_extension_of_hankelColumns hk hcol
  exact hno K hKeq hKan

/-!
# The equivariant Tate exponential sequence and the rationalized Kummer class

On the suspension cover the exponential map carries the suspension parameter in its exponent:
`E_u(α) = exp(2πi α / u)`.  Its kernel is the lattice `uℤ`, which is the Tate local system, and it
is onto the invertible functions, so the exponential sequence is exact.  The factor `u⁻¹` is forced:
a family `exp(2πi c(u) α)` is invariant under the simultaneous scaling of the suspension parameter
and of the weight-one coefficient exactly when `c(u) = c(1)/u`.

Rationalizing the unit group makes the twist and the Frobenius power cancel: on `ℚ ⊗ M` the class
of `q • m` against the Tate fibre `q⁻¹` is the class of `m`.  The kernel of the rationalization is
exactly the torsion, so on a field the kernel of the rationalized Kummer class is exactly the roots
of unity.

* `deningerTateExp_eq_one_iff` : the kernel of the exponential is the Tate lattice `uℤ`.
* `deningerTateExp_surjective`, `deningerTateExp_exact` : the exponential sequence.
* `deningerTateWeight_forced` : the `u⁻¹` factor is forced by equivariance.
* `deningerRationalTwist_cancel` : Frobenius power and Tate twist cancel.
* `deningerRationalization_eq_zero_iff`, `deningerKummerKernel_isTorsion` : injectivity modulo
  torsion.
-/

namespace RHTower

open scoped TensorProduct

section ExponentialSequence

/-- The equivariant exponential of the suspension cover, with the forced `u⁻¹` in the exponent. -/
noncomputable def deningerTateExp (u : ℝ) (α : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.exp (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * α / (u : ℂ))

theorem deningerTateExp_add (u : ℝ) (α β : ℂ) :
    deningerTateExp u (α + β) = deningerTateExp u α * deningerTateExp u β := by
  rw [deningerTateExp, deningerTateExp, deningerTateExp, ← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  ring

theorem deningerTateExp_ne_zero (u : ℝ) (α : ℂ) : deningerTateExp u α ≠ 0 :=
  Complex.exp_ne_zero _

theorem deningerTwoPiI_ne_zero : (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0 := by
  refine mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero two_ne_zero ?_) Complex.I_ne_zero
  exact_mod_cast Real.pi_ne_zero

/-- **The kernel of the exponential is the Tate lattice.**  It is the lattice `uℤ`, which carries
the weight-one action of the positive rationals. -/
theorem deningerTateExp_eq_one_iff {u : ℝ} (hu : u ≠ 0) (α : ℂ) :
    deningerTateExp u α = 1 ↔ ∃ n : ℤ, α = (n : ℂ) * (u : ℂ) := by
  have hu' : (u : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hu
  rw [deningerTateExp, Complex.exp_eq_one_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨n, hn⟩
    refine ⟨n, ?_⟩
    rw [div_eq_iff hu'] at hn
    have h2 : (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) * α
        = (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) * ((n : ℂ) * (u : ℂ)) := by
      rw [hn]
      ring
    exact mul_left_cancel₀ deningerTwoPiI_ne_zero h2
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨n, ?_⟩
    have hdiv : ((n : ℂ) * (u : ℂ)) / (u : ℂ) = (n : ℂ) := by
      field_simp
    rw [mul_div_assoc, hdiv]
    ring

/-- **The exponential is onto the invertible functions.** -/
theorem deningerTateExp_surjective {u : ℝ} (hu : u ≠ 0) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ α : ℂ, deningerTateExp u α = z := by
  have hu' : (u : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hu
  refine ⟨Complex.log z * (u : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I), ?_⟩
  rw [deningerTateExp]
  have hrw : 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I *
      (Complex.log z * (u : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)) / (u : ℂ)
      = Complex.log z := by
    field_simp
  rw [hrw, Complex.exp_log hz]

/-- **The exponential sequence.**  The Tate lattice is exactly the set of coefficients with trivial
exponential. -/
theorem deningerTateExp_exact {u : ℝ} (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    Function.Exact (fun n : ℤ => (n : ℂ) * (u : ℂ)) (fun α : ℂ => deningerTateExp u α - 1) := by
  intro α
  constructor
  · intro hα
    rw [sub_eq_zero] at hα
    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (deningerTateExp_eq_one_iff hu α).mp hα
    exact ⟨n, hn.symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨n, rfl⟩
    rw [sub_eq_zero]
    exact (deningerTateExp_eq_one_iff hu _).mpr ⟨n, rfl⟩

/-- **Equivariance.**  Scaling the suspension parameter and the weight-one coefficient by the same
positive rational leaves the exponential unchanged. -/
theorem deningerTateExp_equivariant {q u : ℝ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (hu : u ≠ 0) (α : ℂ) :
    deningerTateExp (q * u) ((q : ℂ) * α) = deningerTateExp u α := by
  have hq' : (q : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hq
  have _hu' : (u : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hu
  rw [deningerTateExp, deningerTateExp]
  congr 1
  have hcast : ((q * u : ℝ) : ℂ) = (q : ℂ) * (u : ℂ) := by
    push_cast
    ring
  rw [hcast, show 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * ((q : ℂ) * α)
      = (q : ℂ) * (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * α) from by ring,
    mul_div_mul_left _ _ hq']
